signals.title: Instinct Concierge and Meta's Muse both start making real outbound phone calls
signals.summary: Two well-funded consumer AI assistants shipped outbound calling within days of each other: Instinct Concierge (Noah Shinn's ~$10B-valuation startup) now books the restaurant that doesn't take online reservations, gets you on a cancellation list, or fights a cable bill over the phone; Meta's Muse added the same for small-business support. Early access rolling out now, not a demo.
signals.run_with_it_note: Don't rent Instinct or Muse. Build the same 'agent that calls a real person and completes a task' capability on David's own Twilio number using a real-time voice model API (GPT-Live-1, the spark from 2026-09-14's radar, is the obvious pick). Cheap first test: one narrow outbound job this week, e.g. calling back missed marina/tour inquiry voicemails within 5 minutes to book them, on infrastructure David already owns instead of a black-box startup app.

signals.title: Bonsai 2 27B: strong reasoning + multimodal in a 5.9GB, 262K-context, ternary-compressed model
signals.summary: Prism ML shipped a 27B-parameter model compressed to near-lossless quality at a 9x smaller footprint (5.9GB) via ternary weights, with a 262K token context and real multimodal capability. Small enough to run fully offline on ordinary hardware.
signals.run_with_it_note: Open weights, self-hostable, no API bill, no vendor dependency. Cheap first test: download it and point it at a real offline/cheap-inference problem David already has open, like classifying Blink cam stills for the marina fuel watch or triaging boatcam footage, and see if a free local model matches what he's currently paying an API for.

signals.title: Notion ships a Skills API: agent instructions become a portable, git-syncable format
signals.summary: Notion's new Skills API exposes team-written 'skills' (spec-compliant instruction files) over three endpoints, syncable into a GitHub plugin marketplace and readable by Claude, ChatGPT, or Vercel's skills CLI. Skills become a portable asset instead of being locked into one agent's format.
signals.run_with_it_note: David's own moat is exactly this: dozens of hand-built Claude skills (radar, morning-brief, google-ads, kid-coach) that ARE the IP. They already live as plain files he owns, not rented. Cheap first test: try `npx skills` against one existing skill this week and see whether making it portable across agent surfaces (so a team member on ChatGPT or a different tool could run the same skill) is worth the plumbing, without giving up ownership of the underlying files.

signals.title: PostHog details the 6-7 loops that make its product self-driving
signals.summary: PostHog published the specific autonomous-agent loops it runs in production: agents investigate bug/error spikes within minutes and propose fixes by passing findings through workflow steps, no human triggering the investigation. A second real-world data point (after Firecrawl's 'AI software factory' from last week) for agents that watch, diagnose, and act without waiting to be asked.

signals.title: AX: Google DeepMind open-sources an execution runtime built specifically for agent workloads
signals.summary: Open-source runtime for running autonomous agents at scale (isolated sandboxes, workspace auto-setup with git/MCP servers, credentialed network policies, sub-second suspend/resume), positioned as a new infra category distinct from microservices or batch jobs. #3 on HN's front page today at 548 points.

signals.title: Kev: a tiny family of decision models (not chat models) built on Qwen3.5
signals.summary: Show HN for a small, fast model family purpose-built for narrow decisions (classify/route/yes-no) rather than open-ended chat, cheap enough to run constantly. Modest but real traction (187 points).

signals.title: a16z: AI-generated app supply has exploded, adoption/demand has not kept pace
signals.summary: a16z's weekly charts show AI code generation has made shipping an app trivial, but users adopting/keeping any given app has stayed flat, a widening gap between supply and demand.
signals.run_with_it_note: Direct corroboration for the Sentry Tower thesis: don't build new apps into an oversaturated field, rebuild ones with already-proven paid demand. Worth citing when picking Sentry Tower's next target.

signals.title: Show HN: Mini-AGI, a continual-learning model trained on 8GB VRAM
signals.summary: A dynamic continual-learning model trained on consumer-grade VRAM (8GB), posted to HN today with modest early traction (168 points). If it holds up, cheap continual learning without full retraining is a real unlock, but this is a single unverified builder claim.

signals.title: "MCP was always a bad idea?" — a real backlash thread against the agent-tooling standard
signals.summary: A critique of Model Context Protocol gaining real HN traction (211 points) arguing the protocol's design has structural problems. Worth watching since David's own setup runs on a large stack of MCP servers.

signals.title: OpenAI ships Astra for Law: GPT-6 Astra plus legal-specific tools and privacy controls
signals.summary: A vertical version of OpenAI's flagship model for legal work, professional context handling, and privacy controls.
